magic_research_baseline.rule: All magical research uses a 1d20 magic research throw against the magical research target value for the spellcaster's level.
The target value is increased by the difficulty of the task.

task_adjustments.adjustment: Increase target value by the spell's level.
Increase target value by +1 per 5,000gp of construct cost.

modifiers.rule: Add Intelligence bonus to the die roll.
If the caster has Magical Engineering, add proficiency rank.
Add any applicable bonus from a library, workshop, or precious materials.

resolution.success: If modified roll equals or exceeds adjusted target value, research succeeds.
resolution.failure: If modified roll is below adjusted target value, research fails.
resolution.automatic_failure: An unmodified die roll of 1-3 always fails.

failure_costs.rule: Failure loses all precious materials invested.
Failure loses all special components invested.

overview.rule: A spellcaster may experiment to improve chances of successful magical research.
Experimentation grants a bonus to the magic research throw.
If the throw is high enough, experimentation can produce a breakthrough.
If the throw fails, experimentation causes a mishap determined by the method used.

rules.rule: Conventional experimentation can only trigger minor mishaps on failure.
Pioneering experimentation can only trigger major mishaps on failure.
Radical experimentation can only trigger catastrophic mishaps on failure.
Because unmodified 1-3 is always failure, any experimental method carries at least a 15% chance of mishap.

procedure.step: If an experimental research throw fails, determine the appropriate mishap table by research type.
Apply the result from the column matching the mishap severity: minor, major, or catastrophic.
If the result instructs another roll, resolve it on the referenced sub-table or referenced core-rules table.

limits.rule: Conventional experimentation cannot achieve better than a minor breakthrough.
Pioneering experimentation cannot achieve better than a major breakthrough.
Radical experimentation can achieve revolutionary breakthroughs.
If the throw would grant a breakthrough better than the highest one permitted by the caster's level or method, apply the highest breakthrough actually permitted.

research_type.name: creating_crossbreeds
research_type.rule: A breakthrough gives the crossbreed special abilities not present in either progenitor.
These abilities represent unexpected synergies between the progenitors.
Minor grants 1 special ability, major grants 2, revolutionary grants 3.
Major and revolutionary breakthroughs tend to give more powerful abilities.
The Judge may choose appropriate abilities or roll on the Unexpected Abilities table using the die listed by breakthrough level.

research_type.name: creating_constructs
research_type.rule: A breakthrough gives the construct special abilities not present in the formula or sample.
Minor grants 1 special ability, major grants 2, revolutionary grants 3.
Major and revolutionary breakthroughs tend to give more powerful abilities.
The Judge may choose appropriate abilities or roll on the Unexpected Abilities table using the die listed by breakthrough level.

research_type.name: designing_constructs
research_type.rule: Without a breakthrough, a spellcaster can only design constructs with HD no greater than twice class level.
A minor breakthrough increases the design HD limit by 2.
A major breakthrough increases the design HD limit by 6.
A revolutionary breakthrough increases the design HD limit by 12.
Breakthroughs do not increase design time or design cost.
The higher HD still increases the cost and time to actually create the construct.

research_type.name: enchanting_magic_items
research_type.rule: A breakthrough gives the magic item an additional ancillary effect.

minor_effects.rule: Minor ancillary effects include effects comparable to +1 versus a particular monster type or an additional 1st-3rd level spell effect.

major_effects.rule: Notable ancillary effects include effects comparable to +2 versus a particular monster type or a 4th-6th level spell effect.

revolutionary_effects.rule: Powerful ancillary effects include effects comparable to sentience, life_drinking, luck, vorpal, dwarven_throwing, or a 7th-9th level spell effect.

research_type.rule: Any ancillary effect uses the same uses or recharge schedule as the item's primary effect.
The Judge may roll randomly for a spell-like ancillary effect as for a spell scroll, or choose an effect based on the item's context and history.

research_type.name: granting_unlife
research_type.rule: A breakthrough gives the undead unexpected special abilities.
If the undead can reproduce, a breakthrough can create a new undead subtype.
Minor grants 1 special ability, major grants 2, revolutionary grants 3.
Major and revolutionary breakthroughs tend to give more powerful abilities.
The Judge may choose appropriate abilities or roll on the Unexpected Abilities table using the die listed by breakthrough level.

research_type.name: researching_spells
research_type.rule: Breakthroughs increase spell power without increasing actual spell level.
Minor breakthrough raises spell power by 1/2 level.
Major breakthrough raises spell power by 1 full spell level.
Revolutionary breakthrough raises spell power by 2 spell levels.
Once created, such a spell can be learned from spellbooks and scrolls normally by other arcane casters.
Use spell power guidelines to determine the effective power of such spells.

research_type.name: ritual_casting
research_type.rule: Breakthroughs increase ritual spell power using the same scale as researching spells.
The increase applies only to that specific casting instance.

row.effect: Gain magic resistance with target value equal to 20 minus HD.

row.name: charm
row.effect: 3/day, enthrall a target that fails a save vs Spells.

save_modifiers.rule: If creature has 3 HD or less, target saves at +2.
If creature has 9 HD or more, target saves at -2.

row.name: invisibility
row.effect: Creature is naturally invisible and may act freely, including attacking, without becoming visible.

row.name: breath_weapon
row.effect: Gain a dragon-like breath weapon usable 3/day, dealing 1d6 damage per HD; save vs Blast for half damage.
row.rule: Area and special properties follow dragon breath rules.

row.name: flying
row.effect: Gain flight with exploration movement 10 feet per HD.

conditional_rules.rule: If already able to fly, gain dive attacks dealing double damage.
If a dive attack hits a victim smaller than the creature, the victim is grabbed and carried off unless save vs Paralysis succeeds.
If the creature already has a dive attack, re-roll this result.

row.name: poison
row.effect: Victims of primary attack(s) save vs Poison or die.

save_modifiers.rule: If creature has 3 HD or less, victims save at +2.
If creature has 9 HD or more, victims save at -2.

row.name: swallow_attack
row.effect: Can swallow whole victims smaller than itself on an unmodified attack throw of 19 or 20.
row.follow_up: A swallowed victim takes damage each round equal to the creature's most damaging attack until the creature is killed or the victim dies.

row.name: ongoing_damage
row.effect: After hitting a victim, deal each following round damage equal to the creature's most damaging attack.
row.limit: Special effects such as energy drain and poison are not ongoing unless separately present.

row.name: bonus_attack
row.effect: Gain one bonus attack identical to the primary attack.

conditional_rules.rule: If already has infravision, increase it to 90 feet.
If already has 90-foot infravision, re-roll this result.

row.name: regeneration
row.effect: Regenerate like a troll: 3 hp per round unless damaged by fire or acid, and may re-attach lost limbs.

row.name: grab
row.effect: Victims of the primary attack must save vs Paralysis or be grabbed.
row.follow_up: Grabbed victims are helpless until they escape by making a successful save vs Paralysis on their turn.

row.name: aura
row.effect: Gain a damaging aura with radius 2 feet per HD that deals 1d8 damage per round to susceptible creatures.

row.name: paralysis
row.effect: Victims of primary attack(s) save vs Paralysis or are paralyzed for 2d4 turns.

row.name: massive_size
row.effect: HD are doubled and all attacks deal double normal damage.

row.name: acid
row.effect: Successful attacks destroy non-magical armor or clothing. Non-magical weapons that strike the creature dissolve immediately after dealing damage.
row.special_rule: Magical weapons and armor may save using the wearer's save vs Death, adding the item's magical bonus if applicable.

procedure.step: On 1-3, victims who meet the creature's gaze must save vs Petrification or turn to stone.
On 4-6, victims struck by the creature's attacks must save vs Petrification or turn to stone.

row.name: energy_drain
row.effect: Victims of the primary attack lose experience levels.

scaling.rule: If creature has 6 HD or less, drain 1 level.
If creature has 7 HD or more, drain 2 levels.

row.name: spell_like_abilities
row.generation: Generate as for spell scrolls, or select abilities appropriate to the creature's other powers.

general_rules.rule: Re-roll any result that duplicates an ability the creature already has, except where a row says otherwise.
At the Judge's discretion, abilities may be selected instead of rolled if they better fit the creature's existing powers.
At the Judge's discretion, later results may be adjusted to match earlier results.

external_rule_references.reference: Magical research target values by caster level are taken from ACKS core rules.
Mortal Wounds table is used by multiple mishap results.
Tampering with Mortality table is used by necromancy mishaps.
Transformation rules are used if a caster continues play after soul transfer into a construct body.
Reincarnation table is used by magical mutation results 10 and 11.
Dragon breath area and special properties are used by unexpected ability breath_weapon.
Spell power guidelines are used to evaluate effective power for breakthrough-created spells.
